name: Exa
description: Search and web-data APIs for AI applications.
sizeNote: Headcount band is an estimate. Confirm on the company's LinkedIn page.

sources.title: Websets v2
sources.quote: Usage now draws down from your existing Exa credits
sources.note: Websets moved from its own subscription to shared credits. That makes cross-product credit accounting relevant. Exa already operates this system.

sources.title: Introducing Exa 3.0
sources.quote: our new search type, priced at $4 per 1,000 requests
sources.note: Exa Lite introduced a price per thousand requests. Its unit price is public, while its billing costs and vendor plans are unknown.

name: Firecrawl
description: APIs that turn websites into data for AI applications.
persona: Product engineering lead for pricing and credits
sizeNote: Headcount band is an estimate. Confirm on the company's LinkedIn page.

sources.title: Plans and credits
sources.quote: Credits are consumed for each API request, varying by endpoint and feature.
sources.note: Different endpoints consume different amounts of credit. That makes metering rules relevant. The pricing page does not establish how much the current system costs.

sources.title: Firecrawl MCP v3
sources.quote: every plan includes free MCP usage that refreshes daily
sources.note: The MCP release adds a daily allowance across plans. Handling that allowance alongside paid credits is a concrete subject for discovery.

sources.title: Introducing Alexandria and our Series B
sources.quote: We raised a $75M Series B led by Smash Capital
sources.note: Funding and a new product add company context. The announcement discloses neither a billing budget nor an active vendor search.

name: Modal
description: Serverless compute for AI inference, batch jobs, and developer sandboxes.
persona: Engineering lead for usage and billing
sizeNote: Headcount band is an estimate. Confirm on the company's LinkedIn page.

sources.title: Compute pricing
sources.quote: Modal continuously records CPU and memory consumption.
sources.note: CPU and memory consumption are metered. The public rate card establishes billing complexity but does not quantify a potential saving.

sources.title: View invoices directly in the Modal dashboard
sources.quote: Workspace managers can now view all historical invoices in the new Invoices tab under Usage & Billing.
sources.note: The invoice tab is evidence of recent billing-product work. Modal already ships billing features, so any incremental value would need validation.

sources.title: Sandbox cost attribution in the Python SDK
sources.quote: The Python SDK now lets you see your spend more granularly.
sources.note: Customer-visible cost attribution makes spend reconciliation a relevant question. The release does not establish a problem with the current implementation.

name: Browserbase
description: Hosted browser sessions and web APIs for developers.
persona: Product lead for developer plans and usage
sizeNote: Headcount band is an estimate. Confirm on the company's LinkedIn page.

sources.title: Browserbase pricing
sources.note: The Developer plan charges an overage per browser hour. Measuring included usage and overages is relevant. Current operating costs are unknown.

sources.title: Introducing Authenticated Fetch
sources.quote: Authenticated Fetch is available for no additional cost on every plan
sources.note: The feature extends an existing plan entitlement. Its availability can guide a conversation about packaging, but says nothing about vendor selection.

name: Tavily
description: Search, extraction, and research APIs for AI applications.
persona: Product lead for API plans and developer growth
sizeNote: Headcount band is an estimate. Confirm on the company's LinkedIn page.

sources.title: Billing, credits and usage limits
sources.quote: a basic search uses 1 credit and an advanced search uses 2.
sources.note: Search depth changes the credit cost per request. The published rule supports a metering discussion, while implementation effort is unknown.

sources.title: What shipped in October
sources.quote: applications for the Tavily for Startups program are open.
sources.note: The launch included startup credits. Tracking grants alongside purchased credits is a plausible use case. Redemption volume and commercial need are unknown.

sources.title: Tavily is joining Nebius
sources.note: Tavily announced it was joining Nebius. Confirm which team owns commercial tooling before choosing a buyer persona.
